scenes.img: In a palace, a king with a grey beard and gold crown holds up a newborn baby girl in wonder, light falling on her like sunrise.
scenes.text: King Ashvapati prayed for years for a child. A daughter was born, so radiant… he named her after the goddess Savitri.

scenes.img: Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, in an ivory sari with a red border, bows to her father the king, then sets out in a royal chariot with attendants toward distant forests.
scenes.text: When she grew up, no one dared to ask for her hand. So her father said… go, and choose your own husband.

scenes.img: In a forest clearing, Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes in an ivory sari with a red border watches Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes, who carries firewood and an axe and gently guides his blind old father by the hand beside a simple hut.
scenes.text: In a forest, Savitri met Satyavan, a prince whose blind father had lost his kingdom. He cut wood, and cared for his parents. And she chose him.

scenes.img: In the palace, Narada: sage with a white beard, saffron robe, a veena resting on his shoulder raises one finger in warning before the worried king, while Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes listens calmly.
scenes.text: But the sage Narada warned: Satyavan is good, and noble… but he has one year to live. Not a day more.

scenes.img: Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes stands firm with her hand on her heart, speaking with quiet certainty to her father and Narada: sage with a white beard, saffron robe, a veena resting on his shoulder.
scenes.text: Savitri said: I have chosen once. A heart chooses… only once.

scenes.img: Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, now in a plain ochre sari, serves food to an old blind couple outside a simple forest hut, while Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes smiles nearby.
scenes.text: So she married him, left the palace, and lived in the forest, caring for his parents… counting the days in silence.

scenes.img: At night, Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes in a plain ochre sari stands still in prayer beside a small lamp, fasting, eyes closed, determined, the forest dark around her.
scenes.text: Three days before the last day, she began a fast. She did not eat, barely slept… and prayed.

scenes.img: Morning: Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes with his axe walks into the deep forest, and Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes in a plain ochre sari walks close beside him, watching him with quiet worry.
scenes.text: On the last morning, when Satyavan went to cut wood… she went with him.

scenes.img: Afternoon under a great tree: Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes lies with his head in the lap of Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, eyes closing, his axe fallen beside him; she holds his face.
scenes.text: In the afternoon, he said, my head hurts… and lay down with his head in her lap.

scenes.img: Under the tree, Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face appears and stands before Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, who holds the still Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes in her lap and looks up at Yama without fear.
scenes.text: Then she saw him. A dark figure in red, with a crown, and a noose in his hand. Yama… the lord of death.

scenes.img: Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face walks away toward the south carrying a tiny glowing soul, the size of a thumb, in his noose, while Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes kneels by the still body of Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes.
scenes.text: Yama drew out Satyavan’s soul, no bigger than a thumb… and turned toward the south.

scenes.img: On a misty path through a dark forest, Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face walks ahead, and Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes in a plain ochre sari follows him steadily, barefoot.

On the misty path, Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face turns back and raises a hand, telling Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes to go back, while she speaks to him with calm, wise gestures.
scenes.text: Go back, Yama said. You have done all a wife can do. But Savitri kept walking, and spoke of dharma, and friendship, and the good… so wisely, that he stopped.

scenes.img: Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face, softened, holds out an open hand offering a blessing to Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, who stands with folded hands, thinking carefully.
scenes.text: Pleased, Yama offered her boons. Anything but Satyavan’s life. She asked for her father-in-law’s sight… and his kingdom… and sons for her own father.

scenes.img: Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes speaks with a gentle, clever smile, and Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face pauses, realising what she has asked.
scenes.text: Yama granted them all. He offered one more. Then let me have a hundred sons, she said… with Satyavan.

scenes.img: Yama, lord of death: dark green skin, gold crown, red robes, a rope noose in his hand, calm stern face smiles and loosens his noose, releasing the small glowing soul back toward Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, who folds her hands in gratitude.
scenes.text: Yama smiled. He had been out-thought. He loosened the noose… and let Satyavan go.

scenes.img: Evening under the great tree: Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes wakes with his head in the lap of Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes, as if from a long sleep, and she smiles through tears.
scenes.text: In the forest, Satyavan woke with his head in her lap… as if from a long sleep.

scenes.img: Night: Satyavan: young man, clean-shaven, short black hair, simple brown cotton forest clothes and Savitri: young princess, long black hair in a braid, steady dark eyes walk home hand in hand through the forest by lamplight, and outside the hut an old man who can now see opens his arms to them.
scenes.text: They walked home through the dark forest… and found his father could see again.
Krishna says in the Gita… The soul is never born, and it never dies. It does not perish… when the body perishes.
